lines.text: Tiffany sold a fake Aztec skull.
A French dealer offered a crystal skull as an Aztec relic.
He could not sell it in Paris or to Mexico's national museum.
Then the New York jeweler Tiffany acquired it.
Tiffany sold it to the British Museum in 1897.

lines.text: It went on view as an ancient Mexican piece.
Some visitors believed it had healing powers.
In 2008, researchers from Cardiff University and the British Museum studied it.

post.caption: Tiffany sold a fake Aztec skull. A French dealer offered a carved rock crystal skull as an Aztec relic, but he could not sell it in Paris or to Mexico's national museum. Tiffany in New York acquired it and sold it to the British Museum in 1897, where visitors believed it had healing powers. In 2008, researchers from Cardiff University and the British Museum studied it. Tool marks under a microscope came from a spinning wheel unknown in Mexico before the Europeans arrived, and the quartz likely came from Brazil or Madagascar. The likely workshop town is Idar Oberstein in Germany.
